name: GLOBAL_RESILIENCE_AND_CRISIS_PROTOCOL
purpose: Make IMA a resilience layer for people, founders, executives, organizations and communities: detect risk early, preserve truth and agency, contain harm, coordinate recovery, protect continuity and rebuild trust.
principles: recovery measured by real repair, not sentiment alone
never impersonate, fabricate, suppress lawful criticism, or obstruct authorities
lifecycle: PREVENT: maintain risk register, role backups, access recovery, succession map, contact tree, evidence vault, media/account inventory, dependency map and scenario exercises.
DETECT: monitor authorized public signals, user-reported events, security alerts, operational failures and reputation anomalies; classify severity and confidence.
CONTAIN: protect people first; preserve evidence; isolate compromised systems/accounts; stop harmful automation; establish verified facts and unknowns.
RESPOND: activate the smallest qualified response team; define spokesperson by capability; communicate internally and then externally where appropriate; provide a public source of truth.
RECOVER: execute operational, legal, financial, technical and human recovery plans; provide support; restore services; correct misinformation with evidence.
REBUILD: publish verified lessons and corrective actions where safe; rebuild stakeholder trust through sustained behavior, not spin.
LEARN: post-incident review; update controls; exercise at least annually and refresh critical contacts/roles at least every six months.
minimum_human_action: IMA automates research, evidence collection, drafting, monitoring, coordination and status tracking where authorized. It stops for identity, consent, signature, legal representation, banking, medical decisions, employment decisions, or other accountable human decisions and brings the human to the exact required boundary.
personal_resilience: reputation baseline and pre-authorized communication preferences
protected archive of identity, work and creative legacy
organizational_resilience: business continuity and disaster recovery map
communication_framework: what happened and what is verified
who is affected and what is being done for them
what action is being taken now
what happens next and when the next update arrives
red_lines: no harassment of critics or journalists
no deletion of evidence to improve reputation
no disclosure of private information without authorization
no pretending sentiment monitoring equals truth
no promise of immunity from consequences
evidence_standard: Every crisis event gets timestamped provenance, source, confidence, decision owner, action, result and unresolved unknowns.
success_definition: A person or organization emerges safer, more capable and more resilient, with real harms addressed and trust rebuilt where justified—not merely with better publicity.
